numbering_policy: Original Saints references, chapters, reading sections, anchors and continuation bodies are preserved. Missing original verse numbers are not filled from another edition.
review_notes: Read all 73 actual source units in Mark 1–2 from the exact pinned Saints English record, after the parent confirmed that every original Matthew source unit had been read.

Every retained target was read in the exact Saints originals with the surrounding narrative or discourse where needed. Original target ordering, absent-verse gaps and Greek-based book divisions remain intact.

The opening composite citation is handled without silently changing Mark's Isaiah attribution: the messenger clause is compared with Malachi 3:1 and Exodus 23:20, and the wilderness-voice clause with Isaiah 40:3.

Mark's Spirit descending into Him and Matthew's upon Him are kept distinct. Luke's fire in John's baptism saying is not added to Mark, and Mark's wild animals are not inserted into the other wilderness accounts.

The searching groups in Mark and Luke, the healing-summary quantities, the Levi call details, pronouns in the meal complaint and the tile-versus-dug-roof descriptions are qualified rather than harmonized.

The bread episode preserves Mark's Abiathar and the Saints Samuel record's Abimelech, without declaring the priest names identical or importing a different patronymic. Saints 1 Samuel 21:2–7 is used as saved.

A target range counts as one pair. Three sources have additional independently useful targets: Mark 1:2 for the composite wording, Mark 1:13 for angelic ministry alongside the testing setting, and Mark 2:26 for the original bread episode beside the Gospel parallel. Completion still counts each source only once.
The two deferred units receive zero completion credit. The hourly numerical target does not justify a generic connection.
No source wording, display wording, continuations, verse IDs or division membership is edited. This is an AI-assisted English initial passage review, with independent specialist review pending.

All76 actual Mark3–4 source units and every retained target passage were read from the exact Saints cache with surrounding context as needed. Matthew's entire original inventory had been read before Mark source review was authorized.

All74 paired sources have one retained proposal each. Two source units are explicitly deferred with zero completion credit. Source wording, IDs, chapter divisions, and continuation paragraphs are unchanged.

Boanerges/Sons of Thunder remains specific to Mark's list rather than being supplied to Matthew. The given apostolic names match Matthew's actual list; no Thaddaeus/Judas-son-of-James identity claim is needed or imposed.

The boat/crowd-pressure and inability-to-eat comparisons are qualified as different scenes or internal recurring patterns. The insanity accusation comparison does not make John's speakers the same people as Mark's own people.
Sower explanations, good-soil yield order, private explanation contexts, judgment/hearing applications of the measure saying, and lamp-saying locations are kept distinct where the Evangelists differ.

Joel's sickle comparison uses the actual Greek-based Saints reference Joel4:13 and preserves vintage/winepress language against Mark's grain harvest. No other edition's Joel3 numbering was substituted.
The naturally growing seed is not treated as the same parable as Matthew's hostile-darnel parable. The 1Corinthians comparison does not assert that Mark's verse explicitly names God as the grower.

Storm comparisons preserve different addresses, faith rebukes, and boat details without inventing a single wording for the accounts. These are AI-assisted English passage judgments, not independent human specialist or live-destination verification.

All 99 actual Mark 5–6 source units and every retained target passage were read from exact Saints cached snapshots. The 98 proposed completed sources have 98 pairs; Mark 5:5 remains deferred with zero completion credit.

Target IDs resolve, target passages follow contiguous original units, complete source coverage is exact, pair keys are unique, and no target contains its own source unit. Original words, gaps, and continuation structure were preserved.

Exorcism comparisons preserve country versus abyss, whole city versus Decapolis, two-thousand-pig count versus no count, and the difference between reports about the healed man and reports including pigs. No psychological diagnosis or manufactured event sequence is added.

Jairus comparisons distinguish Mark's initially dying daughter from Matthew's already-dead report. Aramaic Talitha koum is not inserted into Luke. Attendance restrictions distinguish accompanying Jesus from entering the room and the parents' participation.
The woman's medical history preserves Mark's worsening after suffering and Luke's no-cure formulation, without presenting the accounts as identical in every detail.

Hometown comparisons preserve carpenter versus craftsman's son, Joses versus Joseph, and could do no mighty work versus did not do many. Mission equipment preserves Mark's permitted staff and sandals versus Matthew's restrictions.
Mark 6:22's exact His daughter Herodias is retained beside Matthew's Herodias's daughter. No unverified identification as Salome or genealogical harmonization is supplied.

Herod's role remains distinct across accounts: Mark describes fear and protection of righteous John with glad but perplexed listening; Matthew describes wanting to kill John but fearing the crowd. Herodias's expressed desire and maternal prompting are not transferred between actors.

Feeding and water-walking comparisons preserve the accounts' withdrawal occasions, Bethsaida destination detail, grouping in hundreds and fifties, green grass, bread question, intention to pass by, Peter sequence, and differing descriptions of the disciples' reactions.
Mark 6:52 to 8:17–21 is explicitly a later same-book recurrence of hardheartedness and failure to understand the loaves, with an actual callback to five loaves, five thousand, and twelve baskets.

This is AI-assisted English passage review, not exhaustive concordance, fresh Greek critical-text or apparatus verification, independent human specialist approval, or live destination-anchor checking.

Read all 122 actual Mark 7–9 source units: 36 in chapter 7, 38 in chapter 8 and 48 in chapter 9. Absent Mark 7:16 and 9:44/46 were not invented, and all original IDs, display text and continuation bodies remain unchanged.

Each retained target is read in the exact pinned Saints source with relevant context. Target ranges include all original units between their declared endpoints; a multi-verse passage counts as one pair.

Related procedures in Mark 7:33 and 8:23 are explicitly same-book comparisons of distinct people and body parts, not claims that the healings are identical. Staged restoration is not silently replaced by another account's immediate sight.

Real differences remain stated: Syrophoenician/Greek versus Canaanite; Dalmanutha versus Magadan; Herod versus Sadducees; sign refusal with or without Jonah's exception; after three days versus on the third day; and prayer versus little faith in the explanations for failed expulsion.

The opening hearing-and-speech restoration comparisons use the actual Isaiah 35:5–6 wording without claiming that Mark explicitly cites it. Jeremiah 5:21 and Isaiah 66:24 retain their Greek-based Saints identities and actual wording.

The crowd, private question and greatness-discussion parallels specify additional or missing details rather than treating every narrative exchange as the same quoted speech. The boy's deathlike condition is not declared actual death.

Source verses with multiple useful targets earn only one distinct-source completion. Deferrals, duplicates and invented counterparts earn none. The numerical hourly target does not justify generic or unsupported links.

Marriage comparisons preserve Mark's reciprocal wife/husband remarriage statement, Matthew's sexual-immorality exception, and Paul's instruction to remain unmarried or reconcile rather than silently unifying the formulations.

The wealth teaching preserves Mark10:24 exactly as supplied, without importing a qualification about those trusting in riches. Present rewards with persecutions and coming-age life remain distinct from Matthew's shorter promise.
Mother-versus-sons requests, cup-and-baptism imagery, first/last saying, and passion prediction wordings are retained as each account gives them.

Jericho comparisons preserve one named Bartimaeus versus Matthew's two unnamed men and Luke's approach to Jericho versus Mark's leaving it. Luke is not made to attest the discarded garment or springing up.
The mount counts, temple-cleansing order, immediate versus later-discovered fig-tree withering, and different evening departure subjects/destinations are explicitly qualified.
Tenant-parable comparisons preserve messenger counts, grouped versus successive missions, the killing/casting-out order, and the listeners' answer versus Jesus' supplied answer.

Direct source quotations retain the supplied Greek-based Psalm117:22–23 and Psalm109:1 numbering and the exact Deuteronomy, Leviticus, and Exodus wording, including Mark's added mind term in the love command compared with Deuteronomy.

The scribe's favorable commandment discussion is not made identical with Matthew's testing motive. The Hosea comparison preserves mercy/knowledge language rather than replacing it with Mark's love wording.

All 175 actual Mark 13–16 source units and every retained target passage were read from the exact Saints cached snapshots, with surrounding context. The 171 proposed completed sources have 175 distinct pairs; four sources remain deferred with zero credit.

All target IDs resolve, passages follow contiguous original target units, source coverage is exact, keys are unique, and no target includes its own source unit. The absent Mark 15:28 is neither invented nor counted.

Mark 16:9–20 is reviewed only as the supplied provisionally authorized source text. Its opening double bracket at 16:9 and closing double bracket at 16:20 are preserved with all original wording and verse identities. This passage review does not claim new critical-text authentication, apparatus verification, UBS6/ECM approval, or independent specialist acceptance of the longer ending.

The Olivet parallels preserve explicit differences including I am he versus I am the Christ, angel-gathering boundaries, omission versus inclusion of a Sabbath flight qualification, and named versus unnamed questioners. No date, present-day identification, or eschatological system is inferred.

The anointing comparisons preserve unnamed critics versus disciples or Judas, more-than-three-hundred versus three-hundred valuation, and John's theft motive as John's detail. The head-anointing and John's feet-anointing contexts are not silently made identical or assigned a synthesized chronology.
Saints Zechariah 13:7 actually uses plural shepherds, a sword command, and tear away the sheep. Those words remain distinct from Mark 14:27's singular shepherd, I will strike, and scattered sheep.

Passover preparation parallels preserve the named Peter-and-John pair in Luke versus two unnamed Mark disciples, the water-jar and upper-room details, and differing meal formulations. Neither supplied blood-of-the-covenant verse is rewritten to insert new.

Peter's denials preserve Mark's twice-crowing prediction and two crow notices, Matthew's unnumbered crow, the same versus another servant girl, and differing Galilean or speech descriptions. The naked young man is left unidentified and deferred.

Mark 15:25 gives the third hour of crucifixion, while John 19:13–16 places the judgment-seat scene at about the sixth hour before handover. The comparison preserves the chronology discrepancy without invented clocks, calendar reconciliation, or one merged timeline.

Passion and burial comparisons retain purple versus scarlet, myrrh versus gall, Eloi versus Eli, inscription and women-list differences, the centurion's different grounds of reaction, and Pilate's verification versus John's soldiers' observations.

Resurrection parallels preserve the spice chronology, sunrise versus dawn, one sitting white-clothed young man versus two standing figures, silence versus joyful reporting, Mark's another-form wording versus Luke's unrecognizing eyes, and differing reception of the returning pair's report.

The Mark 16 sign comparisons are clause-specific: Acts narrates exorcism, tongues, an accidental viper encounter without harm, and healing by hands. It does not provide an event involving drinking a deadly substance, and no such event is fabricated or attributed to Acts.
Mark 16:7 to 14:28 is explicitly an internal promise-and-reminder link. The Acts examples do not convert a local narrative into independent proof of every clause of the supplied Mark ending.
